chunks: So We let loose on them a violent wind for several days of distress to make them taste a most disgraceful punishment here in this world, and far more shameful will be the punishment in the Hereafter, and there will be no succour for them.

key_terms.لَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ: and the punishment of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Rihun Sarṣar in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'violent wind' (Rihun Sarṣar) is often interpreted as a specific, scouring wind that stripped the disbelievers of their dignity, serving as a tangible precursor to the ultimate disgrace of the Hereafter. This verse underscores the concept of 'Azab al-Khazya' (punishment of disgrace), illustrating how divine retribution in the worldly life is merely a shadow of the eternal humiliation awaiting those who are left without divine or human support.
